analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation edit in docs/threat-model.yaml, head lines 1969-1970 (base line 1969). It widens the T-050 mitigation text for inline video ingestion. The text now lists data:video/mp4, data:video/x-m4v, data:video/quicktime and data:video/mov, and adds that the bytes must be an MP4 or QuickTime file. It keeps the decoded-byte, duration, frame-pixel, video-count and aggregate caps, and it keeps rejecting http(s), file and unsupported container MIME types. The supplied base_text units (base lines 898-1873) show surrounding unchanged threats T-010 through T-046, including T-041, but the changed line itself lies outside the supplied base text window. I could not view the changed hunk's surrounding source beyond the patch excerpt. The edit is documentation only. It changes no executable code and no security controls, and it removes no mitigation. I therefore found no concrete regression within the supplied evidence. Open question for integration: the code that implements the MIME allowlist and the byte-sniffing check (the provider media ingestion path) is not supplied here. This pass cannot confirm that it matches the documented behavior. Specifically, it cannot confirm that the new x-m4v and mov MIME aliases and the container-bytes check are enforced fail-closed, or that AVURLAssetReferenceRestrictions.forbidAll and the temp-file handling from T-050 are preserved. If the PR includes provider-swift media changes, the next pass should check those paths against T-050 and T-003/TB-003. The statement that the T-050 affected_files list is still accurate also remains unverified.
